claim: Statistics addition is identified by KDD 2024 as one of the top-performing content optimizations for visibility in generative-engine responses.
sourceCitation: Aggarwal, Murahari, Rajpurohit et al., "GEO: Generative Engine Optimization", KDD 2024 — Statistics Addition is highlighted as a top-performing content-optimization method (§4, Table 1).
notes: The paper does not publish a per-method aggregate lift number we will attribute to this individual recommendation. Headline result reported in the paper is 'up to 41% improvement on Position-Adjusted Word Count' for the best-performing method overall. Per-method numbers previously displayed (e.g. '+33.9%') were not traceable to the paper and have been removed pending an internal benchmark.

claim: Generative engines preferentially cite content with recent dated statistics, treating recency markers as a freshness signal independent of the page's own publish date.
sourceCitation: Practitioner consensus 2025-2026 (Profound, Frase, Search Engine Land); no controlled study located that publishes the specific freshness-citation correlation.
notes: Previously displayed as '83% of commercial AI citations come from sources updated in past 12 months' — that figure is widely repeated in industry blog posts but not traceable to a primary source we can cite. Queue for internal benchmark: re-audit a sample of URLs after their statistics are updated to current-year values and measure citation-count delta.

titleTemplate: Add expert quotes with named attribution
claim: Quotation addition (named-attribution direct quotes from credible sources) is identified by KDD 2024 as one of the top-performing content optimizations for AI-engine visibility.
sourceCitation: Aggarwal, Murahari, Rajpurohit et al., "GEO: Generative Engine Optimization", KDD 2024 — Quotation Addition is highlighted as a top-performing content-optimization method (§4, Table 1).
notes: The paper does not publish a per-method aggregate lift number we will attribute to this individual recommendation. Per-method numbers previously displayed (e.g. '+32%') were not traceable to the paper and have been removed pending an internal benchmark.

titleTemplate: Add 2-5 outbound links to authoritative sources
claim: Adding outbound citations to credible sources (Cite Sources) is identified by KDD 2024 as one of the top-performing content optimizations for AI-engine visibility, with effect size dependent on the page's current SERP position.
sourceCitation: Aggarwal, Murahari, Rajpurohit et al., "GEO: Generative Engine Optimization", KDD 2024 — Cite Sources is highlighted as a top-performing content-optimization method (§4, Table 1); §4.2 / Table 3 reports the effect is strongly conditioned on SERP position.
notes: The paper does not publish a single per-method aggregate lift; instead it reports SERP-position-conditioned effects (e.g. +115.1% visibility for rank-5 sites, -30.3% for rank-1 sites in the Cite Sources experiment). Per-method number previously displayed (e.g. '+30.3%') misread the paper's negative finding for top-ranked sites as a positive lift and has been removed. SERP-conditioned lift is captured as a methodology note for a future product feature; not surfaced as a recommendation lift figure.

titleTemplate: Lead with a 40-60 word direct answer
claim: Generative engines extract opening statements far more often than buried conclusions, making the first paragraph the highest-leverage location for a direct definitional answer.
sourceCitation: Practitioner consensus 2025-2026 (Frase, Profound, Search Engine Land); aligns with classical featured-snippet optimization literature.

titleTemplate: Add 40-60 word answer capsules after each H2
claim: Self-contained 40-60 word answer blocks placed immediately after each H2 are among the most extractable patterns for AI engines, which often lift them verbatim as citation snippets.
sourceCitation: Practitioner consensus 2025-2026 (Frase, Profound, agency case studies); no controlled study located.
notes: Previously displayed as '+35-40% extraction rate' — that figure has no traceable primary source and has been removed. Strong candidate for internal benchmark: A/B test answer-capsule presence against citation-count on our audited corpus.

claim: AI engines treat H2/H3 as a query-map to user prompts; question-phrased headings improve the heading-to-prompt match.
sourceCitation: Practitioner consensus 2025-2026 (Search Engine Land, HubSpot); no controlled study located.

titleTemplate: Add an FAQ section with 10-15 questions
claim: FAQ-formatted Q&A blocks (especially when paired with FAQPage schema) are disproportionately surfaced by AI engines because they pre-match likely user prompts.
sourceCitation: Practitioner consensus 2025-2026 (Frase, HubSpot, Search Engine Land); no controlled study located.
notes: Previously displayed as '+40% citation likelihood' — that figure has no traceable primary source and has been removed. Recommendation kept because the qualitative case is strong and the cost is low.

titleTemplate: Add structured lists or comparison tables
claim: Structured lists, step-by-steps, and comparison tables are heavily favored by AI extractors over dense paragraph prose.
sourceCitation: Practitioner consensus 2025-2026; aligns with featured-snippet extraction patterns documented across SEO literature.

titleTemplate: Add a comparison table (pricing, features, or alternatives)
claim: Agentic search workflows (OpenAI Operator, Perplexity Comet) browse and compare; pages with machine-readable comparison tables are pulled into agent workflows more often than prose-only pages.
sourceCitation: Practitioner observation 2025-2026 (early agentic-search era); no controlled study yet.

claim: Paragraphs over ~120 words are skipped more often by AI extractors than paragraphs of 3-5 sentences.
sourceCitation: Practitioner consensus; aligns with classical readability + featured-snippet guidance.

claim: Comprehensive sources covering related questions, edge cases, and follow-ups are preferred by AI engines over thin pages.
sourceCitation: Practitioner consensus 2025-2026; aligns with topical-authority SEO literature.

titleTemplate: Refresh stale content (last updated ~{age} months ago)
claim: Content older than 24 months earns substantially fewer citations than content updated within the past 12 months. Substantive revisions are detected; cosmetic date bumps are not.
sourceCitation: Practitioner consensus 2025-2026 (Profound, Search Engine Land); no controlled study located.
notes: Previously displayed as '3.2x citation lift moving from >24mo to <12mo' — that figure has no traceable primary source and has been removed. Strong candidate for internal benchmark: we have an audit corpus and can re-audit a sample of URLs after their content is refreshed and measure the citation-count delta.

titleTemplate: Refresh aging content (last updated ~{age} months ago)
claim: Content past the 12-month freshness threshold loses citation share, especially on Perplexity and Google AI Overviews.
sourceCitation: Practitioner consensus 2025-2026 (Profound, Search Engine Land); no controlled study located.
notes: Previously displayed as 'up to 3.2x citation lift returning to <12mo' — that figure has no traceable primary source and has been removed. Same internal-benchmark queue as content-stale-24mo.

titleTemplate: Add a visible "Last Updated" date and current-year markers
claim: Perplexity and Google AI Overviews aggressively deprioritize content with no visible publish date or recent-year reference.
sourceCitation: Practitioner consensus 2025-2026; widely observed but not formally measured.

claim: Year mentions in body copy are weaker than structured datetime metadata; <time> tags and article:published_time meta let AI engines verify recency unambiguously.
sourceCitation: Practitioner consensus; aligns with schema.org best practices and Google's guidance on dated content.

claim: AI engines match entities by literal name; replacing pronouns and "the platform" with the brand name in opening sections improves entity matching.
sourceCitation: Practitioner consensus 2025-2026; aligns with entity-disambiguation literature.

titleTemplate: Add a named-author byline with credentials
claim: Visible author credibility is part of the 2026 baseline for content cited across major AI engines; Claude in particular weights author credentials heavily.
sourceCitation: Practitioner consensus 2025-2026 (HubSpot, Search Engine Land); aligns with Google's E-E-A-T guidance.

claim: Generic filler phrases ("In today's fast-paced world…", "It's important to note…") dilute information density and contribute no extractable claims.
sourceCitation: Practitioner consensus; aligns with general writing-quality best practices.

claim: Traditional keyword-stuffing is actively harmful in generative-engine contexts; AI models penalize obviously over-optimized prose.
sourceCitation: Aggarwal, Murahari, Rajpurohit et al., "GEO: Generative Engine Optimization", KDD 2024 — Keyword Stuffing is identified as a non-performing optimization method (§4, Table 1).
notes: The paper reports Keyword Stuffing as one of the methods that does NOT improve visibility (in some configurations it slightly decreases it). We frame the recommendation as a negative-signal removal rather than a positive-lift intervention. No precise lift number published per method.

claim: Article JSON-LD with author, datePublished, and dateModified enables richer AI extraction and unambiguous metadata interpretation.
sourceCitation: schema.org Article specification + practitioner consensus on AI-engine schema parsing.

claim: Wrapping Q/A pairs in FAQPage JSON-LD remains widely cited as a high-ROI structured-data type for AI citations.
sourceCitation: schema.org FAQPage specification + practitioner consensus.

claim: Organization JSON-LD with sameAs links to social profiles, Wikipedia, and Crunchbase anchors brand identity in the AI knowledge graph.
sourceCitation: schema.org Organization specification + practitioner consensus on entity-disambiguation via sameAs.

claim: The 2026 evidence on llms.txt is mixed; few top-cited domains use one and major engines do not appear to rely on it. Cheap to publish but not a priority.
sourceCitation: Practitioner observation 2025-2026; widely surveyed but not formally evaluated.

claim: If AI engines are blocked in robots.txt, citation in those engines is impossible regardless of content quality. This is a prerequisite, not an optimization.
sourceCitation: Direct mechanical prerequisite — no source needed beyond the robots.txt specification.

claim: Passages that open with a definition or direct answer and stand alone without surrounding context are extracted more reliably by AI engines than passages requiring upstream context.
sourceCitation: AEO Improvement internal heuristic — passage-citability scoring derived from our own audit corpus. Scoring methodology documented on the methodology page; lift number pending controlled benchmark.
notes: Previously displayed a '134-167 word optimal passage length' figure derived from classical featured-snippet length norms, not from controlled measurement against generative engines. Removed pending an internal benchmark; recommendation framed qualitatively in the meantime.
